module purpose: Instruction memory for the core: it accepts bus requests on bus_req_i, forms an index (addr / addr_ff), reads a 32-bit word into rdata from either a pre-initialized ROM (mem_rom_c) or from RAM byte arrays (mem_ram_b0..mem_ram_b3), optionally accepts bus writes into RAM (when IMEM_INIT = false) controlled by bus_req_i.stb/rw/ben and bus_req_i.data, and drives the bus response bus_rsp_o (ack, data, err).

use-case flows.value: memory-write eligibility (bus write strobes & rw decide whether a bus request will write IMEM bytes)
write bytes from bus_req_i.data into RAM byte-arrays mem_ram_b0..mem_ram_b3 on a clock edge when the write guards hold
fetching a 32-bit word: index computed from bus_req_i.addr, rdata assembled from ROM or RAM bytes, and bus_rsp_o.data driven from rdata when rden is asserted
bus response acknowledge event produced on bus_rsp_o.ack according to bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw (and the IMEM_INIT generic)
response-related registers are cleared when rstn_i = '0' (rden and bus_rsp_o.ack forced '0')

conceptual assets.concept: Instruction memory contents (the 32-bit word fetched and delivered on the bus)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The 32-bit word returned to the bus is the module's rdata and is driven out as bus_rsp_o.data when rden='1' (bus_rsp_o.data <= rdata when (rden = '1') else (others => '0'); line 185). rdata is sourced either from the pre-initialized ROM (rdata <= mem_rom_c(to_integer(addr)); line 81 and rdata <= mem_rom_c(to_integer(addr_ff)); line 95) or from the RAM byte-arrays assembled into rdata (rdata(7 downto 0) <= mem_ram_b0(to_integer(addr)); ... rdata(31 downto 24) <= mem_ram_b3(to_integer(addr)); lines 128-131 and the alternative lines 159-162). When IMEM_INIT = false the RAM bytes mem_ram_b0..mem_ram_b3 are written from bus_req_i.data under the write guard ((bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '1')) and gated by bus_req_i.ben (lines 114-126 and 142-155). Therefore the integrity of the stored bytes and of rdata directly determines the instructions fetched and returned (lines cited above); mem_ram_b* exist and are written only in builds where IMEM_INIT = false (map configuration entries).

conceptual assets.concept: Requested address (the bus-provided address used to select which IMEM word is read or written)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The request address enters from bus_req_i.addr and is converted into the local index 'addr' by the concurrent assignment addr <= unsigned(bus_req_i.addr(addr_hi_c downto 2)); (line 101). That index selects which ROM or RAM bytes supply rdata (reads: rdata <= mem_rom_c(to_integer(addr)); line 81; RAM read assignments: lines 128-131; alternative, the registered index addr_ff is clocked (addr_ff <= addr) and used by the alt-style assignments (lines 92, 95, 142, 159-162). Thus the integrity of the bus request address (and of the stored addr_ff when registered) determines which instruction word is fetched (lines 101, 92, 81, 128-131, 159-162).

conceptual assets.concept: Bus response acknowledge (the ack event driven to the requester)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module produces the bus-level acknowledge that reports request completion: in the bus_feedback process rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) (line 176) and bus_rsp_o.ack is driven from bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw under the IMEM_INIT-dependent branches (if IMEM_INIT = true then bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw); else bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb; lines 177-181). bus_rsp_o.ack is also reset to '0' on rstn_i = '0' (line 172-174). The correctness (integrity) of this ack decision matters to bus handshaking and is implemented by these lines and records.

conceptual assets.concept: Read-enable decision rden (the internal read-request latch that gates returned data)
conceptual assets.reasoning: rden is a stored decision set each clock by rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) (line 176) and it is used to gate bus_rsp_o.data (bus_rsp_o.data <= rdata when (rden = '1') else (others => '0'); line 185). Therefore the value held in rden controls whether rdata is presented on the bus and is an established control decision of the module (lines 176 and 185).
